title: Global failures that keep a knot
claim: Global failures that keep a knot. (1) Signed Z4 at four places (x +- y +- z +- w = c mod 4) fails globally on the 6-point 4-regular substrate whose lines are the complements of the edges of a hexagon, and removing any one of its 6 lines leaves 8 solutions with knots of three variables. (2) Signed Z4 at three places fails globally on a 9-point cubic substrate, and removing one of its lines leaves 8 solutions with knots; on all 73 connected cubic substrates with at most 8 points (the 60 census incidence graphs read both ways), under every signing class, its global failures are rigid, so 9 points is the minimum for a cubic signed Z4 space that keeps a knot. (3) Unit-weighted Z8, Z9, Z25 and Z27 laws fail globally and keep a knot on many census substrates. (4) Every removal found that keeps a knot has a non-cyclic solution group, as ticket A requires. So composing like cycles does not force rigid selection: the coset laws of Z_(p^k), k >= 2, which compose like cycles (KNOT-CIRCUITS Theorem 1), have globally failing spaces that keep emergence inside. Checked by brute force over Z4^6 and Z4^9 for the two signed examples, exhaustively over signing classes on the census, and by sampling for the unit-weighted laws.
failure_conditions: Either signed Z4 example not failing globally, or losing every knot after the stated line removals, under brute force.
A non-rigid global failure with a cyclic solution group.
foundation_claim_scope: Existence of non-rigid global failures for Z_(p^k) coset laws; census statistics are sampled for unit weights.
